nodes.title: Cover and contents
nodes.summary:
This section is a formal notification letter dated July 31, 2024, addressed to the National Stock Exchange of India and BSE Limited, announcing the schedule for the company's 21st Annual General Meeting on August 23, 2024. It confirms the electronic distribution of the FY2023-24 Annual Report and AGM Notice in compliance with SEBI regulations, while providing the company’s registered and corporate office details.

The section contains administrative and governance facts, specifically the **AGM date and mode**, **regulatory compliance references** (SEBI Listing Obligations), **distribution method** (electronic vs. physical), and **corporate contact information** (addresses, CIN, and signatory details). The most important facts are the **AGM date** and the **compliance confirmation** regarding the submission of the annual report to the stock exchanges.

nodes.title: Giving wings
nodes.summary:
This section serves as the table of contents and a high-level summary of IndiGo’s FY24 performance, highlighting a record year characterized by significant growth in customer base, revenue, and operational scale. It provides a snapshot of key financial and non-financial metrics, such as 107 million customers, ₹689,043 million in revenue, and a fleet of 367 aircraft, alongside details on sustainability and governance.

The section contains **financial figures** (revenue, profit after tax, EBITDAR, earnings per share), **operational metrics** (passengers/customers, daily flights, load factor, available seat kilometres, destinations), **fleet size**, **employee data** (total employees, women in workforce, training hours), and **growth rates** (year-over-year changes). The most important facts are the **revenue from operations (₹689,043 million)**, **profit after tax (₹81,725 million)**, **customer count (107 million)**, and **fleet size (367 aircraft)**, as these define the company's scale and profitability.

nodes.title: Giving wings  to the nation
nodes.summary:
IndiGo highlights its growth from a single aircraft in 2006 to a current fleet of 367 planes, supported by 985 aircraft on order to secure capacity through the next decade and achieve its goal of becoming a 600+ aircraft carrier by 2030. The section emphasizes the airline’s market leadership in India, citing an 81.3% on-time performance rate in DGCA metros and its commitment to affordable, courteous service to solidify its position as the nation's preferred airline.

The section contains facts and figures related to **fleet size** (current and ordered), **growth targets** (2030 goals), **operational performance** (on-time percentage), and **corporate strategy** (vision, mission, and customer promises). The most important specific figures are the **367 current aircraft**, **985 aircraft on order**, and the **81.3% on-time performance** metric.

nodes.title: Leading the way  towards new  heights and across  new frontiers
nodes.summary:
IndiGo’s FY24 CEO perspective highlights the successful execution of its "Towards new heights and across new frontiers" strategy, marked by a record 500-aircraft order to secure fleet growth through 2030 and an expansion to 33 international destinations. The section also emphasizes operational improvements, such as the introduction of the "6E Eats" catering concept and the "6E χ" transformation initiative, alongside social impact efforts benefiting over 42,000 individuals through the IndiGoReach program.

The section contains facts and figures related to **fleet size** (500-aircraft order, 600+ aircraft target by 2030), **international network expansion** (33 destinations, +7 YoY), **social impact metrics** (41,000 women/children and 1,000 transgender individuals benefited, 1 million tree planting commitment), and **operational performance** (OTP ranking, catering revamp). The most important figures are the **500-aircraft order** and the **33 international destinations**, as they define the company's long-term growth trajectory and market positioning.

nodes.title: Where we operate Connecting the world,  one dot at a time
nodes.summary:
IndiGo’s FY24 annual report highlights its extensive global network, which includes 88 domestic destinations in India and 33 international destinations across regions such as the Middle East, South-East Asia, and newly entered markets in Central Asia and Africa. The airline operates a high-frequency schedule with 13,475 weekly domestic flights and 456 weekly flights to Middle Eastern destinations, supported by codeshare partnerships with eight partners covering over 30 European destinations.

The section primarily contains **network and operational metrics**, specifically:
*   **Destination counts**: 88 domestic and 33 international destinations (including new regions like Central Asia and Africa).
*   **Flight frequency**: 13,475 weekly domestic flights and specific weekly frequencies for key international regions (e.g., 456 to the Middle East, 169 to South-East Asia).
*   **Partnerships**: 8 codeshare partners providing access to 30+ European destinations.
*   **Geographic expansion**: Identification of new regions (Central Asia, Africa) and specific new destinations (e.g., Baku, Tblisi, Nairobi, Almaty, Tashkent).

nodes.title: Key milestones Our incredible journey  so far
nodes.summary:
This section chronicles IndiGo’s growth trajectory from its 2006 inception to FY24, highlighting key operational and financial milestones such as becoming profitable in 2011, going public in 2014, and achieving its highest-ever annual total income in FY2024. It emphasizes recent achievements in 2022–2023, including welcoming over 100 million customers, operating 2,000+ daily flights, and expanding its fleet to over 300 aircraft while serving more than 100 destinations.

The section contains facts and figures related to **fleet size** (100th, 200th, and 300+ aircraft deliveries), **passenger volume** (100 million+ customers), **operational scale** (2,000+ daily flights, 100+ destinations), **financial performance** (highest-ever annual total income in FY2024, profitability milestone), and **strategic partnerships** (codeshare with Turkish Airlines). The most important figures are the **100 million+ customers**, **2,000+ daily flights**, and the record **annual total income in FY2024**, as they underscore the airline’s market dominance and financial success.

nodes.title: Efficiency  at the helm
nodes.summary:
IndiGo’s fleet comprises 367 aircraft, with 78% being Airbus A320neo models that offer a 15% improvement in fuel efficiency, supported by a future order book of 985 aircraft. The airline boasts the youngest fleet in the world among carriers with over 100 aircraft, with an average age of just 4.4 years.

The section contains facts and figures regarding **fleet size**, **fleet composition** (specific aircraft types and counts), **fleet age**, **fuel efficiency**, and **future orders**. The most important figures are the total fleet size (367), the high proportion of fuel-efficient A320neo aircraft (78%), and the record-low average fleet age (4.4 years).

nodes.title: Key performance indicators Financial highlights
nodes.summary:
IndiGo’s FY24 annual report highlights significant financial growth, with revenue from operations reaching ₹689,043 million and an EBITDAR margin of 25.5%, alongside a profit after tax of ₹347,375 million. The section also details operational expansion, noting a fleet size of 367 aircraft, 37,200 employees, and a load factor of 86.2% supported by 139,281 million available seat kilometres.

The section contains the following kinds of facts and figures:
*   **Revenue** (from operations)
*   **Profitability metrics** (EBITDAR margin, Profit after tax)
*   **Liquidity** (Total cash)
*   **Operational capacity** (Available seat kilometres, Fleet size)
*   **Efficiency** (Load factor)
*   **Human resources** (Employees)

The most important figures are **Revenue from operations**, **Profit after tax**, and **Fleet size**, as they directly reflect the company's financial health, profitability, and physical growth capacity.

nodes.title: Ensuring a hassle-free  experience
nodes.summary:
This section highlights IndiGo’s customer-centric initiatives, including the "India by IndiGo" program to connect remote areas, the AI-driven "6Eskai" chatbot for multilingual booking, revamped in-flight catering, and specific support for solo female travelers. It also details the company’s commitment to inclusivity and its strong performance metrics, such as having one of the highest Net Promoter Scores (NPS) in India and a top 10 global ranking for on-time performance.

The section primarily contains **qualitative service descriptions** (e.g., features of 6Eskai, catering menus, community partnerships) and **performance metrics** (specifically NPS and on-time performance rankings), with the most important figures being the **top 10 global on-time performance ranking** and the **high NPS score**.

nodes.title: Powering growth together
nodes.summary:
IndiGo highlights its human capital strategy by emphasizing a diverse and inclusive workforce, noting significant growth in the employment of persons with disabilities to approximately 200 and achieving 44% overall female representation alongside 18% female leadership. The section details various employee engagement and development initiatives, including the "6E Embrace" DEI program, the "6E People Beacon" managerial training for over 1,700 managers, and wellness platforms like "IndiGood Life" and "6E Voice" to foster a supportive corporate culture.

**Kinds of facts and figures contained:**
*   **Workforce Composition & Diversity:** Number of employees with disabilities (approx. 200), percentage of female leadership (18%), and overall female representation (44%).
*   **Employee Development & Training:** Number of managers participating in the "6E People Beacon" program (over 1,700).
*   **Corporate Initiatives & Culture:** Details on DEI strategies ("6E Embrace"), wellness programs ("IndiGood Life"), and internal feedback platforms ("6E Voice").
*   **Operational Milestones:** Completion of 56 projects by the "6E Task Force" since 2018.

**Most important facts:**
*   The specific metrics on **diversity and inclusion** (disability employment growth and gender representation) as they directly relate to the company's stated competitive advantage and UN SDG alignment.
*   The scale of **leadership development** (1,700+ managers trained), indicating a significant investment in human capital capability.

nodes.title: Reaching out to the  community
nodes.summary:
IndiGo’s CSR arm, IndiGoReach, focuses on social responsibility through initiatives in women’s empowerment, environmental sustainability, and cultural heritage preservation, aligning with UN Sustainable Development Goals. Key achievements include reaching 41,000 women and 1,000 transgender individuals with skills training that boosted household incomes, impacting 24,300 households with clean energy technologies like biogas and solar lights, and supporting the restoration of historical monuments across India.

**Kinds of facts and figures contained:**
*   **CSR/Community Impact Metrics:** Number of beneficiaries (41,000 women, 1,000 transgenders, 24,300 households), income increase percentages (20-25%), and percentage of households earning over one lakh rupees (>60%).
*   **Environmental/Emissions Data:** Reduction in fuelwood consumption (55.11%) and traditional fuel use (52%) due to clean technology adoption.
*   **Programme Details:** Specific initiatives (Lakhpati Didi, My City My Heritage), locations (Himachal Pradesh, Indore, New Delhi, etc.), and types of interventions (biogas units, smokeless cookstoves, heritage walks).
*   **Strategic Alignment:** Reference to UN SDGs and corporate social responsibility pillars.

**Most important facts/figures:**
*   **41,000 women and 1,000 transgenders reached** (primary social impact metric).
*   **24,300 households reached** through environmental initiatives (primary environmental impact metric).
*   **55.11% reduction in fuelwood consumption** (key quantified environmental benefit).

nodes.title: 13,500  children benefitted
nodes.summary:
IndiGo’s FY24 report highlights its corporate social responsibility efforts, noting that 13,500 children benefited from education initiatives and detailing employee volunteering activities such as blood donation drives and senior citizen care. The section also outlines the airline’s environmental strategy, emphasizing that 78% of its fleet consists of fuel-efficient Airbus A320neo aircraft, which has contributed to a 19% reduction in CO2 emissions per available seat kilometre since FY2016.

The section contains facts and figures related to **social impact** (number of children benefitted, number of locations for senior citizen care), **fleet composition** (percentage of A320neo aircraft, percentage compliant with Chapter 14 noise standards), and **environmental performance** (CO2 reduction percentage, fuel efficiency improvements). The most important figures are the **13,500 children benefitted** and the **19% reduction in CO2 emissions per available seat kilometre**, as they quantify the core social and environmental achievements of the period.

nodes.title: Turning miles into  milestones

The section emphasizes the airline's industry leadership through accolades from reputable organizations such as SkyTrax, CAPA, Brand Finance, and ch-aviation, which recognize its service quality, fleet youth, and brand strength.

nodes.title: Management Discussion and Analysis
nodes.summary:
The Management Discussion and Analysis section outlines the robust recovery of the Indian aviation sector in FY24, driven by rising middle-class demand and government infrastructure initiatives, while positioning IndiGo as the market leader with over 2,000 daily flights across 121 destinations. It details the company’s strong financial performance, highlighted by a 26.3% increase in passenger ticket revenue to ₹608,227.74 million, alongside strategic initiatives to mitigate risks through fleet modernization, codeshare partnerships, and enhanced cybersecurity measures.

**Kinds of facts and figures contained:**
*   **Financial Performance:** Revenue (specifically passenger ticket revenue and ancillary services), income growth percentages.
*   **Operational Metrics:** Fleet size/composition (e.g., 78% Airbus A320neo family), daily flight count, number of domestic and international destinations, passenger traffic trends (RPKs).
*   **Market & Industry Data:** Global and Indian GDP growth rates, industry recovery levels compared to 2019, government investment figures (e.g., ₹1 trillion for airports).
*   **Risk Management:** Strategies for talent retention, IT/cybersecurity breaches, and environmental compliance (greenhouse gas emissions reduction).
*   **Corporate Strategy:** Codeshare partnerships, international network expansion plans, and sustainability investments (electric ground equipment).

**Most important facts/figures:**
1.  **Passenger Ticket Revenue:** Increased by 26.3% to **₹608,227.74 million** in FY24.
2.  **Operational Scale:** **2,000+ daily flights** across **88 domestic** and **33 international** destinations.
3.  **Fleet Efficiency:** **78%** of the fleet consists of the fuel-efficient Airbus A320neo family.

The Board's Report for FY24 outlines IndiGo’s corporate governance structure, including the functions of its five key board committees, adherence to related party transaction policies, and the implementation of a whistle-blower mechanism to ensure ethical conduct. It also details operational highlights such as a 28% increase in staff training at the in-house facility iFly, the adoption of fuel-saving policies, and the company’s CSR activities under the IndiGoReach initiative.

*   **Human Resources/Training:** Specific metrics on employee training (28% increase in headcount trained, ~120,000 individual programs completed).
*   **Operational/Sustainability:** Fuel efficiency policies (e.g., Eco-Power Engine Wash).
*   **Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR):** Financial details on CSR spending and unspent amounts.
*   **Financial/Statutory:** References to audited financial statements, loans/investments/guarantees, and directors' responsibility statements.

*   **Training Metrics:** The 28% increase in trained headcount and the completion of nearly 120,000 training programs at iFly.
*   **Governance Structure:** The existence and specific roles of the five Board committees (Audit, Nomination & Remuneration, Risk Management, CSR, and Stakeholders Relationship).

nodes.title: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (pages 99-122)
nodes.summary:
IndiGo’s FY24 Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report highlights its commitment to operational sustainability, such as electrifying ground operations at Ahmedabad, and its extensive market reach across 33 Indian states/UTs and 24 international countries. The section also details corporate governance metrics, including employee turnover rates, grievance redressal mechanisms, and a comprehensive analysis of material risks and opportunities with their associated financial implications.

The section contains facts and figures related to **market presence** (number of states and countries served), **human resources** (employee turnover rates), **sustainability initiatives** (electrification of ground equipment), **governance** (grievance complaint statistics), and **risk management** (identification of material risks/opportunities and their financial implications). The most important figures are the **market coverage** (33 domestic locations, 24 international countries) and the **material risk/opportunity assessments**, as these define the company's operational footprint and strategic resilience.

nodes.title: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (pages 123-140)
nodes.summary:
This section of IndiGo’s FY24 annual report details the company’s Business Responsibility and Sustainability (BRS) performance, highlighting zero data breaches, nil Scope 3 emissions, and specific metrics on waste intensity and supplier sourcing from MSMEs. It also outlines governance mechanisms for stakeholder consultation, human rights grievance redressal, and the company’s affiliations with industry bodies.

The section contains facts and figures related to **sustainability metrics** (waste intensity, air emissions, Scope 3 emissions), **social responsibility** (employee grievances, rehabilitation of injured workers, NGO partnerships), **supply chain** (percentage of inputs sourced from MSMEs), and **governance** (stakeholder consultation processes, data breach incidents). The most important figures include the **waste intensity per rupee of turnover**, the **percentage of input material sourced from MSMEs**, and the confirmation of **zero data breaches** and **nil Scope 3 emissions**.

nodes.title: Independent Auditor's Report
nodes.summary:
The Independent Auditor’s Report provides an unqualified opinion on the standalone financial statements of InterGlobe Aviation Limited for FY24, confirming that they present a true and fair view of the company's financial position and performance in accordance with applicable accounting standards. Additionally, the report details the auditor’s assessment of key audit matters, such as lease accounting and tax implications, while verifying compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, including the absence of material fraud and the adequacy of internal financial controls.

The section primarily contains **audit opinions**, **key audit matters** (specifically regarding lease accounting and tax), **legal and regulatory compliance statements** (including details on dues paid under protest and pending disputes), and **internal control assessments**. The most important facts are the **unqualified audit opinion** and the confirmation of **no material fraud** or significant non-compliance with statutory requirements.

nodes.title: Standalone Financial Statements

The section contains balance sheet data (assets, liabilities, equity), profit and loss figures (revenue, expenses, profit), equity changes (share capital, reserves), and cash flow statements (operating, investing, financing activities). The most important facts and figures include the pre-tax profit, total income/expenses, depreciation and amortisation expenses, interest on lease liabilities, and cash and cash equivalents at the beginning and end of the year.

nodes.summary:
This section of the annual report provides a statutory disclosure (Form AOC-1) detailing the salient financial features of IndiGo’s newly incorporated wholly-owned subsidiary, InterGlobe Aviation Financial Services IFSC Private Limited, which was acquired on October 12, 2023. It specifies the subsidiary’s reporting period (October 12, 2023, to March 31, 2024) and its capital structure, noting an authorized capital of ₹300 million and a paid-up capital of ₹0.1 million.

The section contains corporate governance and structural facts, specifically listing the **Board of Directors** (including the Chairman, Independent Directors, and Managing Director), the **subsidiary’s share capital** (authorized and paid-up amounts), and the **acquisition date** of the subsidiary.

nodes.title: Notice of Annual General Meeting
nodes.summary:
The Notice of the 21st Annual General Meeting for InterGlobe Aviation Limited, scheduled for August 23, 2024, outlines the agenda for shareholder approval, including the re-appointment of statutory auditors and directors, as well as an increase in borrowing limits. The section provides detailed procedural instructions for remote e-voting and participation via video conferencing, along with an explanatory statement and annexures detailing the qualifications and shareholdings of directors seeking re-appointment.

The section primarily contains **governance and procedural facts**, specifically:
*   **Board/Directors:** Details on the re-appointment of specific directors (Mr. Anil Parashar and Ms. Pallavi Shardul Shroff), including their DINs, dates of appointment, and shareholdings.
*   **Auditors:** Information regarding the re-appointment of M/s S.R. Batliboi & Co. LLP as Statutory Auditors.
*   **Financial Limits:** A proposal to increase borrowing limits and create charges against borrowings.
*   **Procedural/Regulatory:** Instructions for remote e-voting, video conferencing access, and compliance with SEBI LODR and Companies Act regulations.

*Note: This section does not contain operational financial figures such as revenue, profit, passenger counts, fleet size, employee numbers, emissions, or dividend details.*
